entries.title: video 2 design brief and specification
entries.creator: Mr Gilbert - DT
entries.watchFor: Listen for the difference between a design brief and a specification. Note how a designer turns the intended user, purpose and research into requirements that can guide later decisions.
entries.relevance: A concise secondary D&T lesson that supports the section’s user, purpose and requirement thinking. It does not set this course’s project brief or assessment requirements.

entries.title: The Elements of Fashion Design
entries.creator: Catherine Sews
entries.watchFor: Track each element—line, shape, colour, texture and pattern—and pause when the presenter explains how a visible choice changes the effect of a garment.
entries.relevance: A fashion-specific overview that broadens the former line-only clip and directly supports identifying and explaining design elements.

entries.title: The Principles of Fashion Design
entries.creator: Catherine Sews
entries.watchFor: Notice how emphasis, proportion, balance, rhythm and harmony organise visible elements. At the final gown example, name the evidence before accepting the judgement.
entries.relevance: A fashion-specific principles overview with an applied garment analysis. The section theory remains the authority for the course’s full seven-principle set.

entries.title: From Ideation to Printed Fabric | My 6 Step Process
entries.creator: Mel Armstrong - Illustrator
entries.watchFor: Track how an initial idea is researched, developed, tested and refined before it becomes a textile design.
entries.relevance: Supports design development and purposeful refinement; the course theory remains the authority for focus areas and design factors.

entries.title: How to read a Sewing Pattern for Beginners
entries.creator: Tock Custom
entries.watchFor: Pause on the envelope, pattern pieces and common symbols. Match each marking to the information it communicates.
entries.relevance: Supports commercial-pattern interpretation. Students must still follow the teacher-issued pattern, instructions and local safety controls.

entries.title: Behind the Scenes: A day in the life of a Textile Designer
entries.creator: The Careers Department
entries.watchFor: Notice the different visual, written and digital ways the designer communicates ideas to other people.
entries.relevance: Provides a real communication context without prescribing the class project.

entries.title: The Complete Fashion Design to Production Process
entries.creator: FittDesign Studio
entries.watchFor: Identify where planning, refinement, quality checks and evaluation appear across the development process.
entries.relevance: Provides a broad production context; students use their teacher’s current project brief and requirements.

entries.title: Fibres to Fabrics — Introduction and types of fibres
entries.creator: Sri Chaitanya Academy NEET
entries.watchFor: Follow the hierarchy from fibre to yarn to fabric and note the broad natural and manufactured classifications.
entries.relevance: A concise orientation beside the course’s more detailed fibre classification and structure theory.

entries.title: Classification of Textile Fibres
entries.creator: Textile Vlog
entries.watchFor: Sort the examples by origin and production, then compare that classification with the natural, regenerated and synthetic groups in the module.
entries.relevance: Reinforces classification; fibre properties and lifecycle judgements must still use the course evidence.

entries.title: Yarn manufacture from staple fibres: twist and its effect
entries.creator: Vidya-mitra
entries.watchFor: Notice how fibres are aligned and twisted, and how changing twist alters the yarn rather than simply changing its appearance.
entries.relevance: Supports staple-spun yarn formation and twist relationships.

entries.title: Textile Yarns — Twisting and Plying
entries.creator: Textile with Alberto
entries.watchFor: Identify single and plied structures, then predict how construction may change strength, balance and handle.
entries.relevance: Supports structure–property reasoning and end-use justification.

entries.title: The 3 Fundamental Textile Weaves: Plain, Twill and Satin
entries.creator: Textile with Alberto
entries.watchFor: Compare the interlacement repeat in plain, twill and satin rather than relying only on surface appearance.
entries.relevance: Directly supports the woven-structure section; knitted and non-woven structures remain in the adjacent course theory.

entries.title: FIT's Textile-Testing Lab
entries.creator: Fashion Institute of Technology
entries.watchFor: Look for controlled conditions, repeatable measurement and the connection between a test result and a product decision.
entries.relevance: Shows professional testing context without setting the school’s apparatus, method or WHS controls.

entries.title: Testing of textile fabrics: objectives
entries.creator: Vidya-mitra
entries.watchFor: Identify why a property is tested and how results can support selection, comparison and quality decisions.
entries.relevance: Supports using experimental evidence in Project 2 while the teacher-approved practical method remains authoritative.

entries.title: Textile: From Fibers to Fashion | Industry Supply Chain Explained
entries.creator: suppliersplatform
entries.watchFor: Map the stages from materials through manufacture and distribution, then identify how one change can affect several stages.
entries.relevance: A broad value-chain view used alongside current Australian industry and training sources.

entries.title: Behind the Seams: Ensuring Quality at Every Step from Design to Delivery
entries.creator: Hold-True
entries.watchFor: Separate actions that prevent defects from checks that detect defects, and note where evidence is recorded.
entries.relevance: Supports quality assurance and control; it is an industry example rather than a required class process.

entries.title: Mastering Exam Command Terms
entries.creator: School of Learning
entries.watchFor: Listen for how command words change the depth and structure of a response, then compare the advice with this module’s exact definitions.
entries.relevance: Supports response planning. The course theory and the teacher’s issued assessment notice remain authoritative.
